prompt: Given a skyline of one-unit-wide columns, work out how deep the rainwater sits on each column and how much is trapped in total. Complete waterPerColumn and totalTrapped in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: The depth over column i depends on the tallest column at or to its left and the tallest at or to its right -- the water can only rise to the lower of those two walls. Recomputing those maxima inside a nested loop works but is slow; instead one left-to-right pass fills a tallestLeft array and one right-to-left pass fills tallestRight, after which a third pass computes min(left, right) - height and clamps negatives to zero. The end columns always get zero because one of their two walls is the column itself.
hints: Write down the formula for one column first: depth = min(tallest at or left of i, tallest at or right of i) - heights[i], clamped at 0. Everything else is just supplying those two maxima.

Precompute them into two arrays. A forward pass fills the tallest so far from the left -- each entry is the larger of the previous entry and the current height -- and a backward pass fills the right side the same way from the end.
Handle the small cases before you allocate anything: null means an empty result, and any array shorter than 3 columns is already all zeros.
